title: Localization: the map, her position and the scene
tagline: Where she, the monsters and other players are, in the game's own map units
summary: Localization turns what perception saw on screen into places on the map. It reads each map's layout and art straight from the game's data files, works out where the character stands (from her minimap dot refined on screen, or since 2026-10-30 exactly, from the camera registered against the map's art plus a filter over her name tag, plate and body), and places monsters, drops and other players on their platforms. Every look the rest of the stack decides on passes through `Senses`, which hands out a `Scene`: one frame placed on the map.
details_md:
**Map units.** Everything is measured in the game's world units ("map units"): x to the right, y downward. The game lays out a 1366x768 view at one unit per game px and stretches it to its window (1.40625x at 1920x1080).

**The map** (`mapdata`, `mapart`). The map model comes from the game's own WZ files (the client's packed data archives) through the repo's `gamedata` package, kept off git. A *foothold* is one straight line segment of ground in the map data; platforms are footholds chained end to end, plus walls, ropes, portals, spawn points and each monster's EXP, body, speed, touch damage and HP. A platform lying on another is its *twin* and counts as that platform. `mapart` draws the map's fixed art (tiles, objects, backgrounds) as one picture so the camera can be registered against it.

**Her place, two ways.**

| | the dot path (`pose`) | the scene path (`locate`) |
|---|---|---|
| where | 1920x1080, the simulator, maps without art, first frames | 1366x768 with her plate model and the map's art (default since 2026-10-30) |
| her map place | minimap dot (11.4 units a px) snapped to a platform | registered view + her feet on screen |
| refined by | her tag on a fixed camera, a rope in view, her platform's end | tag template, plate colours, body pose bank, a Kalman filter |
| accuracy | about 11 units, better when refined | within 3 px on every held-out frame |

On the scene path `camreg` finds the camera's exact view each frame by matching gray sample rows against the map's art, `locate` finds her with the cheapest cue that works and carries her through frames where none does (counting frames under the Lie Detector (the game's anti-bot check, whose windows cover the play area), her stat window or a portal's light as *covered*, not lost), and her minimap dot stays a coarse check. `her_cues` builds her tag template, plate model and pose bank offline. On both paths `placecheck` rejects a place off the map (outside the map's VR box, the rectangle the camera never shows past).

**Looks** (`senses`, `scene`, `rate`). Perception runs as a separate process (the perception service) and steps its world model on every frame, 15 a second (`rate.HZ`). `Senses.look` returns the newest state that is fresh enough (shown after her last key's effect, at most 0.1 s old), retries looks that fail their checks and raises `LookLost` after 3 s, then runs listeners (EXP and HP bookkeeping, telemetry) and checks (the safety stop). `Senses.place` is how the world step places a frame. A `Scene` converts screen px to map units through the registered view (or her offset), places monsters on platforms and finds drops in strips above the ground.

**Others on the map.** `monsters` places detections on platforms (exact feet snap or the kind's spawn platforms), predicts where a monster can be (walking on, turning 20 units from its platform's ends) and names which monster an EXP gain killed. `unseen` adds the monsters the feed or her memory knows are near but the look missed: the detector is nearly blind close to her. `players` follows other players' minimap dots and says which rival could have taken a kill.

The rest of the `localization` package (the continuous feed and perception service, the frame-by-frame tracker, the world state, her memory of monsters, EXP gains, aggro, the spawn clock) builds on these modules and is described with the continuous feed. The package may import only perception and the shared modules (`tests/test_architecture.py`).

modules.title: Map data (mapdata)
modules.tagline: Each map's platforms, walls, ropes, portals, spawns and monster stats, read from the game files
modules.summary: Reads a map out of the game's own WZ data (through the repo's `gamedata` package) and builds a `MapModel`: platforms made of footholds chained end to end, walls, ropes and ladders, portals, monster spawn points and per-monster stats (EXP, body size, walk speed, touch damage, hops, HP and defences). Every other module measures in this model's map units, and asks it geometric questions: which platform is under a point, which platforms no monster can touch, how many monsters the server keeps, where a portal's light shines.
modules.details_md:
**Map units.** The game's world units: x to the right, y downward. The game lays out a 1366x768 view at one game px per unit and stretches it to its window (1.40625x at 1920x1080), so wherever screen px are involved the look's `screen.Geometry` converts.

**Reading** (`load`). The parsed map is cached as JSON in `gamedata/data/out/maps/<id>.json`. If it's missing, or was written before the death-animation key existed, `load` reads the map image (`Map/Map/Map*/Map*_000.wz`), `Physics.img`, the map's name (`String/Map.img`) and, for every monster that spawns there, its `Mob/<id>.img`: name, EXP, body boxes, die1 frame delays, speed stat, touch damage (`PADamage`), whether it has a jump or fly action, the highest its body reaches, `maxHP`, `PDDamage`, `MDDamage`, `eva` and `level` (following a mob's `link` where its own data is empty). Caches written before the touch or HP keys existed are topped up in memory but **not** rewritten, because one cache can serve several checkouts at once. Speeds are the exception: a cache without them gets them added and written back (`_add_speeds`), through a `.part` file and `os.replace` so a reader never sees half of it.

**Platforms** (`_platforms`). Every foothold (`foothold/<layer>/<group>/<id>`) is flattened. Vertical ones are walls. Walkable ones are visited left to right and each chain is followed through its `next` link while the next foothold starts where this one ends. Chains are sorted by their left end's height (top first), then x, and a platform's id is its index. Each `Segment` keeps its foothold group (the client's collisions in the air and what stops a star go by it), `forbidFallDown` (`no_drop`) and its neighbours' ends. `parse` then attaches to each platform its group's walls, every floor of the map and all its peers (for `attack.reach`).

**Twins.** A platform lying on another's footholds, within its ends and `TWIN_DY` (2 units) of its surface all along, is a *twin*: for everything the stack does it is the longer one (`twins`, `place_of`, `places`). West Rocky Mountain II has two (11 on 14, 21 on 22). `platform_under` and `platform_below` only look at `places`, so a twin is never their answer.

**Monsters.** `spawn_points` puts each spawn on the platform under it (within `SPAWN_REACH`, 60). `safe(pid)` is true when no monster spawns on the platform and no spawn platform runs under it within `MONSTER_REACH` (55 units: their bodies stick up that far). Walk speed is `walkSpeed` (125 units/s) x (1 + speed stat / 100): pigs 125, slimes 100, snails 43.75. `mob_cap(users)` is the server's monster cap as OrionAlpha's `LifePool.init` computes it: one monster per `CAP_AREA` (128,000 square units) of the box about the map's footholds and walls (each foothold `CAP_BOX_X` 30 inside across, 300 over its top, 10 under its bottom; clipped to the VR box where the map sets `VRLimit`; grown 10 each side), its height less `CAP_SCREEN_DY` (450) and both sides at least the 800x600 screen (`CAP_SCREEN`), times `mobRate`, 1 to `CAP_MOST` (40); with more than half that many users on the map, more, up to twice. Tree Dungeon II gives 22.

**Portals.** `PORTAL_BOX` is the client's take-a-portal box (25 across, 100 above, 25 below its point), read from HeavenClient. `portal_light` composites a portal's animation frames from `MapHelper.img` into its lit box (alpha over 64) and its dense rows (lit across half its width or more); `portal_lights` places them at each visible or hidden portal of a map, and `locate.Cover` uses them to count a frame where she stands in a portal's light as covered.

**Minimap picture.** `minimap_picture` loads the map's miniMap canvas, which perception matches to find where the minimap is drawn. `render` draws the model to a PNG for a person to look at.

modules.title: Map art (mapart)
modules.tagline: The map's fixed tiles, objects and backgrounds drawn as one picture in map units
modules.summary: Draws a map's own art from the game data the way the client does (backgrounds behind, layers 0-7 of objects then tiles, backgrounds in front) into one RGB picture covering every view the camera can take, plus a `static` mask of the pixels that are fixed art only. Camera registration (`camreg`) compares each frame against it; the body cue in `locate` uses it as the background behind her. Cached per map in `gamelab/lab/mapart/<map>.npz`.
modules.details_md:
**Drawing order** (HeavenClient's `MapBackgrounds` and `MapTilesObjs`): backgrounds with `front` 0, then for each layer 0-7 its objects (sorted by `z`, then as listed) and its tiles (by their picture's `z`, or the tile's `zM` where that's 0), then the front backgrounds. Each picture is placed with its origin on its (x, y); flipped objects and backgrounds are mirrored about their origin. A background repeats every `cx` (`cy`) units across (down) by its type: `TILE_X` = {1, 3, 4, 6, 7}, `TILE_Y` = {2, 3, 5, 6, 7}.

**What isn't static.** Some pieces are drawn but marked not static, so registration ignores the pixels they touch: animated objects (more than one frame, or a frame whose alpha changes, drawn with the first frame), backgrounds that don't move 1:1 with the map (by the client's formula only `rx = ry = -100` does, and not a type 4-7 that moves by itself: `back_moves`), animated backgrounds, and pictures `gamedata` can't decode yet (drawn opaque, of unknown colour). Objects whose every frame is invisible (a0 = a1 = 0, foothold carriers) aren't drawn. `_blend` keeps, per pixel, how much of its colour comes from non-static pieces; a pixel is `static` where that is under `UNSURE` (1/255).

**Extent.** `views(info)` gives the range of the camera's top-left from the VR box; on a map no wider (taller) than the 1366x768 view the camera is centred and fixed that way (`MapArt.fixed`), the same rule as `pose.Camera.corner`. The picture spans from the first view's corner to the last view's corner plus the view.

**Cache.** `load` returns the in-memory copy of the latest map, else reads `lab/mapart/<map>.npz` if its key matches (the code's `VERSION` plus the sizes and modification times of the Obj, Tile and Back WZ files, their `_Canvas` picture files, and the Map WZ files), else draws and saves it through a `.tmp.npz` then replace. Only the latest map's art stays in memory (`_LOADED`: Tree Dungeon's is 14 MB, Ellinia's 56); `forget()` lets it go before another is read.

**Checked against frames** (2026-10-29): at the true view of 634 Tree Dungeon frames the best offset was (0, 0) on every one, 96% of the static play area within 2 gray levels, 99.98% of what nothing is drawn over. What the game draws over the map (monsters, players, NPCs, portals, drops, names, effects, the HUD) isn't drawn here; registration's truncated cost absorbs it.

CLI: `python -m gamelab.localization.mapart MAP_ID [OUT.png]` writes the picture and its static mask (default `lab/shots/mapart_<id>.png`) and prints its extent, views and static share.

modules.title: Pose from the minimap (pose)
modules.tagline: Her map position from her minimap dot, refined on screen; the camera model
modules.summary: The original way to place her, still used wherever the scene locator isn't (1920x1080, the simulator, maps without drawable art, the first frames of a map). `Localizer` converts her minimap dot to map units and snaps it to a platform; `refine` tightens her x from her name tag on a fixed camera, a rope in view or her platform's visible end. `Camera` predicts which part of the map is on screen so she can be put on screen when her name tag is hidden. Its `Where` is the position type used everywhere.
modules.details_md:
**Dot to map.** The minimap is the map at 1/2^mag (mag 4 = 1/16), shown 1.40625x larger at 1920x1080, so one minimap px is 16 / 1.40625 = 11.4 map units (16 at 1366x768: `per_px`). `to_map(dot)` = (dot - origin) x per_px - centre, with the map's miniMap `centerX`/`centerY` and `DOT_ORIGIN` (65.1, 91.3) full-size px, fitted at map 10000012 so the dot maps to her feet. `use(geo)` moves the origin to the same game px in another window size; `anchor` refits it from a spot whose map position is known.

**Snapping** (`where_dot`). The dot is good to about 1 px (11 units). Of the platforms covering x (+-15) whose surface is from `FEET_BELOW` (8) above to `DOT_SNAP_REACH` (50) below a point `DOT_SNAP_LIFT` (25) above the dot, it takes the one whose surface is nearest the dot's own height, then clamps x to it and puts y on its line. Only platforms that are places count (`MapModel.places`: never a twin). Once it's chosen, before the clamp, `on_rope_under` catches the rope-top hang: her dot more than `ROPE_TOP_GAP` (17) under the platform's surface, within `ROPE_TOP_X` (16) of a rope hanging from that platform (its top within `ROPE_TOP_DY` 20 of the surface) and above its bottom, and not at standing height on another platform, means she's on the rope: `platform` None.

**Refining x** (`refine`), best source first; each needs her name tag and a platform under her, and must agree with the dot within `DOT_AGREE` (45 units):
- `camera_x`: on a map no wider than the view the camera can't move across, so her tag's screen x gives her map x exactly (to a px).
- `rope_x`: ropes are drawn exactly at their map x; every rope seen within `ROPE_MATCH_PX` (40 full-size px) of where the dot predicts gives an estimate, the median wins.
- `edge_x`: her platform's visible end(s), from the ground extent under her, corrected by `GRASS_OVERHANG` (-24 px: the real ends are 21-27 px past where the grass seems to end), not within `SCREEN_EDGE_PX` (12) of the screen's side.
The source is reported as `how` ('camera', 'rope', 'edge' or 'dot').

**Camera.** The game keeps her at a fixed screen spot (`CAMERA_OFFSET` (674, 489) map units from the top-left) except that it never shows past the VR box, where it stops; on a map no wider (taller) than the view it's centred and fixed (`_axis`). `corner(x, y)` gives the view's top-left for her feet at (x, y), `to_screen` maps a point, `fixed` says which axes can't move, and `learn` nudges the offset 20% (`CAMERA_LEARN_RATE`) toward where her tag was seen, in each direction the camera isn't stopped at an edge (`CAMERA_STOPPED` 0.5).

modules.title: Camera registration (camreg)
modules.tagline: Finds the camera's exact view each frame by matching the screen against the map's art
modules.summary: `Registration.see(frame)` returns the map point at the frame's top-left (`View`), so anything on screen converts exactly to map units (screen = map - view, one unit a px at 1366x768). It compares gray sample rows of the frame against the map's art (`mapart`) at candidate views with a truncated absolute difference, searching outward from a prediction and falling back to a coarse-to-fine search of the whole map. The inner loop is C (`gamelab/camreg.c`, AVX2) with an identical numpy fallback.
modules.details_md:
**The cost.** The frame is sampled every `ROW_EVERY` (6th) row above the HUD (`HUD_TOP` 700), all columns, as gray = avg(avg(r, b), g) with rounding averages, which is the same for RGB and BGR. For a candidate view the cost is the mean of min(|frame - art|, `TRUNC` = 24) over the compared pixels: those in play (not the minimap box or the quest helper: `EXCLUDE`) and static in the art. Anything that isn't the map (her, monsters, names, chat, effects) costs at most 24 a pixel, so at the true view the cost is about 24 x the share covered (0.5-1.4 on the clips) and a px off it is about 3 more.

**The search** (`see`):
1. Predict: the last sure view moved on by its last velocity (px a second when frames carry times), clamped to where the camera can be.
2. Search within `FIRST` (3) px (where the camera moves both ways, a 3x3 and a cross: 17 views; taken only if the best isn't on the window's edge), then `NEAR` (12), then `WIDE` (48). Where the camera moves both ways a big window is searched as a column at the predicted x, a row at the best y, then a 5x5 about that. Each window's cheapest is *settled* (`_settled`): it walks to a cheaper 3x3 neighbour up to `SETTLE` (3) steps.
3. A view is **sure** with cost <= `COST_OK` (16) and the cheapest view 2+ px away at least `MARGIN_OK` (0.6) dearer.
4. Otherwise `cold`: the frame and the art in 4x4 block means (`COARSE`), every view a block apart costed on every 2nd block row, the `COLD_BEST` (4) best distinct picks refined at full size over every 4th sample row, the best settled. On a map the camera scrolls both ways a hint (the camera corner her minimap dot implies) limits it to +-`HINT_R` (64) px; the unhinted whole map (80-900 ms there) is searched at most every `COLD_WHOLE_S` (2 s) while the view is lost, and at once on the first lost frame only when no hint was given. Where the camera moves one way only (Tree Dungeon: 4-6 ms) the whole map is searched on every lost frame.
5. Nothing sure: the prediction is *carried* (`sure` False, `how` "carried"), or "none" before any view was ever placed.

**Speed.** A tracked frame is 0.2-0.4 ms in C against 10-20 ms in numpy; `cr_shrink` shrinks a frame's play area in 0.05 ms where numpy took 13-15. `lib()` builds and loads the DLL once (`native.build`) under a lock; `why` says why it isn't in use.

**Accuracy** (README, Localization): on three clips (10,068 frames) the view was exact on every frame, against the old live camera's 5 px median. It is never sure on a capture shifted off the client, a black frame or another map's frame (margins 0.004-0.06 against 0.6); with 30% of the play area painted over it was still sure and right on every frame.

CLI: `python -m gamelab.localization.camreg MAP_ID PICTURE.png [...]` prints each picture's view, cost and margin from a cold start.

modules.title: The scene locator (locate)
modules.tagline: Her exact place each frame: the registered camera, three on-screen cues and a Kalman filter
modules.summary: `Locator.see(frame, t, dot)` places her to within a few px on every frame at 1366x768: the camera's view from `camreg`, her feet on screen from the cheapest cue that finds her (name tag template, then her name plate's exact colours, then her body against a pose bank), and a filter that carries her through frames where nothing finds her. Her map place is view + screen place. Since 2026-10-30 the perception service places her by it wherever her plate model and the map's art are available.
modules.details_md:
The localization prototype of 2026-10-29, its plate and body cues ported to C (`gamelab/locate.c`, via `perception.plate` and `perception.poses`). Words: her *tag* is the name label the game draws under her; her *plate* is the decorated frame her name-tag item draws round it, whose exact colours identify her; her *pose bank* holds calibrated pictures of her body in each pose.

**A frame** (`see`):
1. More than `GAP_S` (0.5 s) since the last frame: `forget`, start afresh. Else `_rate` updates `k`, the frames per prototype frame (1/15 s) that its counts scale by (1 at today's 15 a second).
2. The camera: `reg.see(frame, t, hint)`, the hint being `Camera.corner` of her dot's map place. Never registered yet: return None (placed the old way).
3. Predict the filter by dt (`_predict`, then `wall_clamp` against vertical footholds).
4. Measure (`measure`), cheapest first, each only if the one before failed:
   - **tag**: her gray tag template in a window sized from the filter's uncertainty (3 sd + 14 across, `WIN_MIN` (24, 36) to 90), then `NEAR` (110, 100) about the prediction; sure at `SURE` 0.85 or the plate model's lower bank level. When lost (never placed, `LOST_N` 4 frames placed by nothing, or her dot's alarm), or once every `FULL_EVERY` (30) frames her tag isn't surely found: the whole play area down to `ROWS_MAX` 700, peaks kept only where her dot agrees.
   - **plate**: `Plate.near` counts her plate's exact colours about the prediction, refused unless her dot agrees (`PLATE_DOT`); lost, `Plate.verify` checks the gray peaks anywhere.
   - **body**: `BodyFinder.find` against her pose bank in the box the filter's uncertainty gives; after `SPRITE_WIDE_AFTER` (2) frames placed by nothing, also a box +-40 px across and +-`WIDE_DOT_Y` (60) about her dot, at most every `WIDE_EVERY` (8) frames and not after the tracked search took `WIDE_BUDGET_MS` (12 ms). Places her at `SPRITE_OK` 0.60, surely at 0.80; her lying-down pose (under `PRONE_H` 55 rows) only with her feet within `PRONE_LINE` (8 px) of a platform's line.
5. Update (`update`, `update_y`). x and its speed are a constant-velocity Kalman filter (`KF1`); y is in one of three modes. *ground*: y on her platform's line, speed capped at `WALK_MAX` (200 units/s); a rise past `TAKEOFF` (2.5 px; `BODY_OFF_LINE` 8 for body-only answers) takes off at the speed that rise implies (`takeoff_v`); feet below it put her on another platform within 4 px, onto a rope at its top, or into a drop; a walk off an end only if tag or plate placed her within `WALK_OFF_SEEN_S` (0.25 s). *air*: gravity (`GRAVITY` 2000) to `FALL_SPEED` 670, landing on the first line crossed; *rope* near a rope when her last three measured places show steady vertical motion (`kin`: |acc| <= `ROPE_ACC` 700, |v| <= `ROPE_VY` 220) or a slowed rise. *rope*: steady y; onto the platform at its top; off when x drifts 8, she is 30 above its top, below its bottom + `ROPE_END` (5), or a fall shows (acc >= `FALL_ACC` 1200). A tag or plate answer 60+ px from the prediction resets the filter there.
6. **Her minimap dot** is always a coarse check: on a frame no cue placed her, a filter place more than `DOT_BOX` (12, 12) from the dot (its `DOT_LAG_S` 66 ms lag allowed for) is pulled to the box's edge; more than `DOT_ALARM` (45 units) away for `DOT_ALARM_N` (3) frames she's lost, and after `DOT_TO_N` (3) carried frames far from it she's put where it is. An unregistered view is re-anchored by her feet on a line (`v_anchor`, `reanchor`).
7. Nothing placed her: `Cover` says whether she's *covered* (the Lie Detector, her stat window, a portal's light) rather than *carried*. Only the count and the scene's `how` change.
8. `output` returns a `Located`; confidence is the cue's score, or when carried 0.5 x 0.8 per prototype frame unseen.

**Where it's used.** `build` makes one only at 1366x768, with `config.toml`'s `[perception] scene` true (default `ON`), her plate model in her lab folder (no pose bank: no body cue) and the map's art drawable; anything building raises is logged and gives None. `Senses._locator` hands it to the eyes; `Eyes.look_at` calls `see` every frame and drops the locator for good if it raises anything but the missing-template RuntimeError.

modules.title: Her cues' calibration (her_cues)
modules.tagline: Builds her name-tag template, plate model and pose bank from saved frames
modules.summary: An offline calibration command that makes the models `locate` needs from a folder of lossless PNG frames: a gray name-tag template cut from her plate, her plate model (`perception.plate.PlateModel`) with her feet's offset, and her pose bank (`perception.poses.PoseBank`). It writes them to her lab folder (or any folder), where `locate.build` and NameTag read them.
modules.details_md:
Input: a folder of lossless frames (PNG, as the golden clips are) with an `index.jsonl` giving each frame's file and time (`frames_of`; without one, the PNGs by name, 1/15 s apart). Exact colours matter: both models are made of them, so the rolling recorder's JPEGs won't do.

**Steps** (`build`), each logged and summarised in `her_cues.json`:
1. Her current full gray tag template matched on every frame (`survey`, `gray_peaks` k=4); its sure levels from its own scores (`plate.sure_levels`), her plate's first model from the sure frames (`plate.pick_centres`).
2. A new tag template cut from that model's median picture (her letters, 2 px around: `plate.tag_template`), the model re-centred on it; every frame matched again, the camera's view of each frame registered against the map's art (`camreg` on `mapart`, sure views only), the plate model made again.
3. Her feet's offset from the plate's centre: across, the plate's own axis (the middle of its stable columns, `PlateModel.axis`); down, `feet_below`: for each frame with a sure tag and a sure view, the platform line under her within `FEET_RANGE` (-40 to -4 px) of the centre, the commonest whole offset if `FEET_SURE` (half) of them agree.
4. Her pose bank from frames where the new tag is sure (its bank level, no other peak within `OTHER` 0.3, its centre `EDGE` 8 px above the HUD) and the view is sure: `poses.build_bank` cuts her from the map's art behind her, with her feet on a platform's line (`ON_LINE` 2 units). Her poses' mirror axis is compared with the plate's; a difference of `AXIS_WARN` (1 px) or more is logged as a warning.

`--keep-tag` skips step 2 (the views are then registered in step 1's pass). `--no-bank` makes the plate model alone: no camera, no map art, so no views, no feet offset measured down (the model's default stays) and no pose bank.

BugBaby's build of 10-30 (2,401 frames, 276 s): her old text tag's template scored 0.882 typical on her plate; the one cut from it is 52 x 15 and 0.996 typical; her feet (-2.5, -16) from it; her poses' mirror axis +0.0 px from her plate's.

CLI: `python -m gamelab.localization.her_cues FRAMES_DIR (--out DIR | --lab) [--map 10002073] [--every N] [--no-bank] [--keep-tag]`.

modules.title: Place check (placecheck)
modules.tagline: Rejects a place read off her minimap dot that lies outside the map
modules.summary: `off_map(model, where)` says, in words for the log, why a place isn't on the map, or None if it is: outside the VR box (or the platforms' and ropes' reach) by more than `OFF_X` (20 units) left or right or `OFF_Y` (50) above or below. Senses doesn't place such a look; it's asked again and after 3 s raises LookLost.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** At 16:46:50 on 2026-10-24 every one of a hunt's 1,148 looks put her 92-956 units right of Tree Dungeon's right edge: her dot was read without the map's minimap picture, with the first map's origin, and the hunt sent a plan off a rope every 5 s for two minutes. On that day's other tours there (7,634 looks) she was always 100 units or more inside its sides and 212 or more inside its top and bottom.

**The edges** (`edges`) are the map's VR box (where the camera stops, which the game keeps her inside), or where its platforms and ropes reach if it has none. The margins allow for her dot's accuracy (about 11 units, a minimap pixel); every bad look of 16:46:50 was further out than either.

**Not checked.** A place in the right map but wrong within it (the minimap picture found at a wrong place) passes. Whether there's a platform or a rope under her was weighed and left out: in mid-air off a platform there can be nothing under her for hundreds of units, and a look in mid-fall taken for a bad one would hold the hunt up.

It is called from `Senses._place_her` and `Senses._by_scene` for both ways of placing her; the frame's own checks are in `perception.framecheck`.

modules.title: Senses (senses)
modules.tagline: The one door every look goes through: the freshest perception state, placed and checked
modules.summary: `Senses.look()` returns the newest perception state fresh enough to decide on, as a `Scene`, from the feed (the perception service in a live command, `SyncFeed` in the simulator, `InlineFeed` on saved frames). It enforces freshness, retries looks that fail their checks and raises `LookLost` after 3 s, runs listeners and checks after each look, and offers `glance()` for a per-frame dot and HP. For the world step it places observations on the map (`place`), by the scene locator or by her dot.
modules.details_md:
**Where looks come from.** Since 2026-10-25 every look is the latest state of the continuous feed: perception runs its world step on every frame (15 a second, `rate.HZ`) and Senses picks a state. Without a feed given, an `InlineFeed` runs the world step on the eyes' own frame when a look asks (made lazily, so the world step's own Senses makes none). The old self-looking mode (`--no-feed`) and Senses' own sweep of the screen a slice a look for her memory were removed then; a look at her band now carries the monsters the feed follows off it in `Scene.swept`.

**Freshness** (`fresh_after`): the newest state of a frame shown after the last look's frame, `KEY_EFFECT_S` (68 ms) after her last key (the game acts on a key 66-68 ms after it's sent; `KEYS_WAIT` "all"), and at most `MAX_AGE_S` (0.1 s) old. A look for monsters also waits for the frame that would show her last throw's kill (`shows`), when that is at most the character's `shows_wait_s` away (`SHOWS_WAIT_S` 0.45 for the thief), asked `SHOWS_LEAD_S` (0.05 s) before it. `after` asks for a frame shown then or later instead. Once the window fix has set the client right, no look or glance takes a frame shown before the window settled (`settled`).

**When there's nothing to act on.** `feed.look` gives None (no state in time, or the state failed `perception.framecheck` or `placecheck`). Then: the `waits` run, the game is brought forward (unless `hands_off`), a window fault Alt+Enter twice can mend goes to `window_fix` (`_mend`), the failure is logged once per reason and sent as a telemetry event, and after `LOST_S` (3 s) `LookLost` is raised, unless the window fix has yet to make its first try (`_fixing`). Retries are `RETRY_GAP_S` (0.2 s) apart. `regain` stands still, looking every `PAUSE_POLL_S` (0.5 s), until a look passes.

**After a look:** her newest touch is noted, the camera learns from her tag, the feed's players are adopted, `rows` filled if missing, the feed's events up to the look's frame attached (`drain_events`), then every listener (the hunter's EXP and HP bookkeeping, telemetry) and every check (which may raise out of the look: the safety stop).

**Glances** (`glance`): her dot and HP from the newest frame (every frame: `FEED_GLANCE_EVERY_S` 0), the state kept in `glanced` for a running chain of keys to react to, and the `glance_checks` run on it (the hunter's HP watch). No state for `GLANCE_LOST_S` (0.3 s) raises LookLost, which cuts a running chain.

**Touches.** Each state's newest touch is kept (`touch`) and its listeners told; `invulnerable_until` is that touch's popup time plus `INVULNERABLE_S` (1.45 s), ignoring `crowded` ones (a MISS that may be another player's).

**Placing** (`place`, used by the world step): `Scene.of(obs)`, then `_place_her`. With the eyes' locator's answer (`located`), `_by_scene` places her by it: the feet's map place, platform, cue, mode and confidence; not found yet, her dot snapped and put on screen by the view (`how` "dot"). Otherwise `Localizer.where_dot`, `off_map`, `refine`, and the camera learns from her tag or puts her on screen. Then `Players.update` with the other dots, only when her own dot was read. `search` asks the eyes for monsters in her band (or the whole screen) and places them.

The locator (`_locator`) is only built for eyes at 1366x768 with a name tag and a real screen. `_rope_columns` has the eyes search for ropes only `ROPE_PAD` (40 + 12 px) about where her dot puts the map's ropes: 8.6 ms a look against 19 for the whole screen.

modules.title: The Scene (scene)
modules.tagline: One look placed on the map: her, monsters, drops, players, and px-to-map conversions
modules.summary: `Scene` extends perception's `Observation` with everything placed on the map: her `Where`, how it was found and how sure, the monsters (`Monster`), monsters swept off her band, drops (`Loot`), other players, and the feed's events, touches and tracks. Its `map_x`/`screen_x` conversions go through the registered view when there is one, else through the offset from her. It also finds drops on the ground (`drop_strips`, `find_loot`) and writes the 'scene' telemetry record.
modules.details_md:
**Conversions.** With a registered view (`view`: the map point at the frame's top-left) map = view + px x `units_per_px`. Without, offsets from her: her tag's x (`tag`) and her feet's row (`floor_y`) against her map place; the camera doesn't scale, so offsets from her hold anywhere on screen.

**Placing a monster** (`place`). Its map x and y come from its foot x and feet y on screen. `monster_platform` picks its platform: an exact feet snap (within 12 units of a surface) when the matched template knows its origin and she's grounded or the view is sure, else the nearest platform where its kind spawns. It's kept within that platform's ends.

**Grounded.** With the locator's mode: tag seen, mode 'ground', on a platform. Otherwise: tag seen, on a platform, and at least `GROUNDED_PX` (6 half-size px) of ground under her feet. In the air every monster's y is off by her height above where her dot puts her (up to her 77-unit jump), unless the view is registered.

**Drops.** `level_runs` splits a platform into nearly level stretches (rising or falling 20 units at most). `drop_strips` makes a strip just above each stretch of her platform (every platform in view with `wide`), `STRIP_PAD` (4) past each end, trimmed above the bottom bar and right of the minimap, skipping ones narrower than `MIN_STRIP` (12) or shorter than an item. `whole` marks a strip not cut by the bar or the screen's top: a cut strip finding nothing doesn't say the drop is gone. `find_loot` asks `eyes.items_in` for items in those boxes, places each on its strip's platform, notes `looked`, and `_on_nearest_platform` keeps one per item (within `SAME_ITEM` 4 px) on the platform whose ground is nearest its bottom.

**Fields from the continuous feed:** `events` (EXP gains, hits, deaths since the last look), `touch` (her newest touch), `tracks` (the feed's monster tracks: live, hidden on screen up to HIDE_S, or just dead), `strips` (drop strips, each searched at its own time), `seq` (the service's frame number). `swept` holds monsters perception follows off her band, re-found in this frame, for her memory; fights go by `monsters`. `landing` and `what_if` mark looks at a landing inside a chain and looks made up from another.

**Record.** `record()` is the 'scene' telemetry topic: her place (`how`, `seen`, `grounded`, and `mode`, `conf`, `view_sure` from the locator), HP and MP, monsters, swept, rows searched, loot, `searched`, `wide`, `looked`, the view box, players and the minimap picture's match.

modules.title: The frame rate (rate)
modules.tagline: HZ = 15: the one rate perception looks at the game, everything once a frame
modules.summary: A single constant, `HZ = 15.0` frames a second. Every frame gets one pass of the perception service's world step (her look and the whole screen's search at once, her place, vitals and touches, monsters matched to tracks, their bars and deaths, the drops), so what the stack reads of the game is never more than a frame and a pass old. Whatever counts frames takes its rate from here.
modules.details_md:
**Who reads it:** `localization.feed.HZ` (and through it `service.HZ` and the simulator's `SyncFeed`), `tracking`, `worldstate`, Senses' glances, `control.recording.FPS`, `control.lie_tracking.FPS`, `control.navigator` and `behavior.targeting`. Change it in this one place.

**History.** 30 a second from 2026-10-26 (the frame loop re-finding followed monsters every frame, the whole screen on a thread of its own every other frame) until 2026-10-30; 15 since, one pass a frame. On the crowd's replay (900 frames, Idle priority on CPUs 12-23) the pass took 0.50 cores at the live rate where the step at 30 took at least 0.75, and every state has its own frame's whole screen, where at 30 the newest whole screen was 70 ms old (median).

What used to be counted in frames at 30 a second is counted in time now (`tracking.MIN_SEEN_S`, `worldstate.BAR_EVERY_S`, `perception.deaths.EVERY_S`); the touch rules were measured on recordings at 15 a second, and the locator's counts are the prototype's at 15 (`locate`: k = 1).

modules.title: Monsters on the map (monsters)
modules.tagline: Monsters placed on platforms, told apart look to look, and predicted ahead
modules.summary: Turns perception's `Mob` detections into `Monster`s on the map's platforms, tells a monster seen again from a new one, and predicts where one can be a moment later (`MonsterTrack`) for the move planner. It holds the monster tables (speed, body, death time) that game data overrides per map, the shared walk-edge rule, and which of the monsters she threw at died when her EXP went up (`dead_one`).
modules.details_md:
**Which platform** (`monster_platform`). With exact feet (the matched template knows its origin; she's grounded or the view is registered) a monster goes on whatever platform's surface is within `FEET_SNAP` (12 units): such feet were -1.4 to +2.5 off on 15 saved frames, against -8.5 to +16.4 by the template's bottom. Otherwise only platforms where its kind spawns count (or any spawn platform), within 50 units: feet read from a template's bottom were about 20 units off at times and once put pigs on a safe platform above them. Within `PLATFORM_SLACK` (25) of a platform's ends.

**Speeds and bodies.** `speeds(model)` and `bodies(model)` start from the tables (`MONSTER_SPEED`: pig and Orange Mushroom 125, slime 100, snail 43.75 units/s; `MONSTER_HALF`, `MONSTER_TOP`, `MONSTER_FLINCH_TOP`, `MONSTER_DIE_S`) and take the map's game data where it has the kind. `walk_vx` turns perception's heading (facing and pose: a move frame) into a velocity at the kind's game-data speed; a stand or flinch frame is 0. `touch_box` is half its width and its tallest walking or flinching height.

**Walk edges** (`walk_edges`). A walking monster turns `WALK_EDGE` (20 units) along the end foothold from each end of its platform, as the v83 client does; one that jumps walks to the ends. Shared by the danger, flow, tracking and probe code and the simulator.

**Prediction** (`MonsterTrack`). `at(t, p)` walks it on at its velocity and bounces it between the walk edges (a monster never walks off its platform: it turns). `reach(t, p)` is where it can be: seen walking, about `at` with `TURN_SLACK` (25) + 20 units a second of spread, and its full speed past `trust`; heading unknown, its speed either way (only `TURN_SLACK` back against a known heading), capped by `unsure`. `reach_over(t0, t1)` adds the end it turns back at in between.

**Look to look** (`Tracker.update`): each monster is matched to the last look's on the same platform within `MATCH_DX` (90) if that look was under `MATCH_WITHIN` (2 s) ago; heading from the move (over `STILL_DX` 6) and speed measured when the looks are `MIN_SPEED_DT` (0.2 s) apart, clamped to the kind's speed. `WALK_MATCH` and `FACING_HEADING` (matching by where it was walking, heading from its facing) are off. This is the navigator's and the hunt loop's tracker; the perception service follows monsters frame by frame with ids in `localization.tracking`, whose id rides on `Monster.track`.

**Same one, dead one.** `same` is the same kind within `TRACK_SLACK` (85) across and `SAME_DY` (40) up or down. `seen_again` prefers the feed's track id when there is one. `dead_one` names which of her targets her EXP gain was: the first of that kind in the path of the throw keyed `GAIN_AFTER_KEY` (0.1-0.6 s) before the gain, seen or not; else one no longer seen nearest her; else the nearest.

modules.title: Unseen monsters (unseen)
modules.tagline: Monsters known to be about that this look didn't find, placed where they likely are
modules.summary: `unseen(scene, memory, model)` returns the monsters she knows are about but the look missed: the perception service's tracks out of sight on screen (hidden, or live but missed in this frame) and her memory's monsters seen in the last 2 s, each placed where it likely is at the look's time. Her fights, her landings for a pile and her trips treat them as part of the look.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** The monster detector is nearly blind near her. Live on 2026-10-25 on Tree Dungeon, of the frames in which the service followed a monster on her platform, 7-12% found it within 50 units of her, 20-34% at 50-100, 44-55% beyond; none of 1,317 searched looks had one within 25 units. 22 of her 34 touches came from a monster no look had in the 0.6 s before, and one Horny Mushroom caused 6 of them and a fall.

**Which tracks count** (`hidden`): a track on a platform that is HIDDEN, or (`UNSEEN_LIVE`, since 2026-11-03) LIVE but last seen before this frame, last seen within `TRACK_S` (1.5 s), not `owed` (the likely target of an EXP gain still waiting), and not one a kill of hers is on (`_hers`). Not every hidden track is a monster: the feed keeps one hidden 1.8 s while it waits to put her EXP gain on it, and up to 3.5 s for one killed by others or lost. 1.5 s is where one was still about as likely there as not (79% seen again at 0.5-1.0 s, 38% at 2.0-2.5).

**Her kills** (`_hers`): for each kill recent enough, its own track (the ledger's), else the track of its kind on its platform nearest where it was placed, within `KILL_NEAR` (80 units), seen about when it was killed. One kill, one track.

**Where each is.** A track walks on at its followed velocity (clamped to its kind's speed; under `STILL_VX` 15 units/s it stands), turning back at its platform's ends (`MonsterTrack.at`). A memory entry (at least `memory.SURE` likely, seen within `UNSEEN_S` 2 s) stays where it was seen.

**Not twice** (`_is_one`). A track or memory entry is dropped if a monster the look found (of its kind, on its platform) is within `MATCH_SLACK` (40) + `MATCH_SPEED` (1.3) x its speed x its age (age capped at `MATCH_WALK_S`, 30 s; all three are `memory`'s): it's that one. A memory entry is also checked against the tracks already added. A LIVE track is compared only with found monsters that have no track of their own, since the tracker already matched the frame's sightings within its gate.

From 2026-11-04 what she shoots goes by `behavior.presence`: these say what's about, not what's worth a throw.

modules.title: Other players (players)
modules.tagline: Other players' minimap dots, placed on the map and followed from look to look
modules.summary: The minimap shows every player on the map, so every look sees them all. `Players.update` places each other player's dot as hers is placed (`pose.Localizer`, snapped to the platform under it), matches dots to the players of the look before, and confirms or drops them over a few looks. `near_rival` finds a rival (anyone not in her party) close enough to have killed a monster: kill attribution and pile decisions go by it.
modules.details_md:
**Placing.** Each marker (`perception.minimap.Marker`: kind and core position, full-size px) is shifted by `other_shift` (their cores are drawn half a game px right of and below hers) and placed with `Localizer.where_dot`, so it lands on a platform the same way hers does.

**Matching** (`update`). Dots are paired with the existing players nearest first, same kind only, within `MATCH_PX` (4 full-size px) plus `MATCH_PX_S` (15 px a second) of time since the last look, capped at `MATCH_MAX_PX` (40; farther it's a new dot: a portal or teleport). A dot is a player once seen in `CONFIRM` (2) looks in a row; a player is dropped once missed in `MISSES` (2) looks in a row **and** for `MISS_S` (1 s), because her marker drawn over theirs as she walks past hides it for about half a second; a dot seen once and missed is dropped at once. `current` returns copies of the confirmed players.

**The feed.** A look from the feed brings the players its own frames followed; `adopt` takes them as they are (ids and all), so a look placed here after it goes on from them. Senses gives its own `Players` ids from `LOCAL_IDS` when a feed is in use, to keep them apart.

**Rivals.** `RIVALS` = stranger, guild, buddy: anyone not in her party (her party's kills near her share their EXP with her). `near_rival(players, x, y)` returns the nearest rival within `REACH_X` (400) across and `REACH_DY` (100) up or down: about a star's reach (434) and a step, a guess since other classes' reach isn't known. `localization.tracking` and `behavior.ledger` use it to tell whose kill a death was; `behavior.hunt` has optional uses (leaving their piles, discounting their ground), both off by the harness's numbers.

flows.title: How a frame becomes her place (the scene path)
flows.summary: At 1366x768 with her plate model and the map's art, every frame of the perception service places her by the registered camera and her on-screen cues.
flows.trigger: Each frame of the perception service's world step (15 a second)

steps.text: Reads her minimap dot and the other players' dots, then asks the eyes' locator for this frame (`_located` -> `Locator.see`).
Starts afresh after a 0.5 s gap, updates the frame-rate factor k, and builds the camera hint from her dot's map place.
Finds the view: about the predicted one (3, 12, 48 px), else cold (coarse blocks, then full size); sure or carried.
Tries her tag template, then her plate's exact colours, then her body against her pose bank; the first that finds her gives her feet on screen.
Folds the measurement into the filter (x Kalman, y by mode: ground, air, rope) and checks it against her minimap dot's box and alarm.
If nothing placed her: is she under the Lie Detector, her stat window or a portal's light (covered) or just carried?
Returns a Located: view, feet, map x/y, platform, mode, cue and confidence; the eyes put it on the Observation.
The world step's Senses.place turns it into her Where, rejecting places off the map (placecheck), and records how and how sure.
Every monster, drop and window in the frame is converted to map units through the registered view.

flows.title: Her place from her minimap dot (where the locator isn't used)
flows.summary: At 1920x1080, in the simulator, on maps without drawable art, or before the camera's first registration, her minimap dot places her, refined by what's on screen.
flows.trigger: Senses.place on an Observation without a Located

steps.text: Takes her dot from the Observation and the look's geometry.
Dot to map units (11.4 units a minimap px at 1920x1080), snapped to the platform whose surface is nearest the dot's height.
Her dot more than 17 under a platform by a rope hanging from it: she's on the rope, no platform.
A place more than 20 units left or right of the map's edges, or 50 above or below, isn't placed: the look fails its checks (Problem "place").
Her x from her tag on a fixed camera, a rope in view, or her platform's visible end, if within 45 units of the dot.
With her tag seen the camera learns where it keeps her; hidden, Camera.to_screen puts her on screen instead.
The other players' dots are placed the same way and matched to the last look's.

flows.title: What happens when the stack asks for a look
flows.summary: Senses.look picks the freshest acceptable state from the feed, retries or gives up when there is none, and runs listeners and checks.
flows.trigger: Any decision that needs a look: a fight's next throw, the navigator, the hunt loop, the mover

steps.text: The soonest a usable frame may have been shown: after the last look, 68 ms after her last key, at most 0.1 s ago.
A look for monsters waits (up to 0.45 s for the thief) for the frame that shows her last throw's kill.
The newest state matching the ask becomes a Scene, with the monsters off her band in `swept`; None if there's none or it failed its checks.

No state: in Senses.look's loop the waits run, the game is brought forward and the window fix tried; _failed logs the problem once per reason and raises LookLost once it has lasted 3 s; otherwise the look is retried 0.2 s later.
A passed look: the camera learns, the feed's players are adopted, the feed's events attached, then every listener and check (which may raise).

flows.title: Monsters about that the look didn't find
flows.summary: The hunt's decisions add to a look the monsters the feed or her memory says are near but this frame missed.
flows.trigger: behavior.hunt, grind, attacks and looting asking for what's about (unseen); control.navigator asking for hidden tracks

steps.text: The feed's tracks on a platform, hidden or live-but-missed, last seen within 1.5 s, not owed and not one her kill is on.
Each recent kill of hers claims one track: its own, or the nearest of its kind within 80 units seen about then.
A track or memory entry within 40 + 1.3 x speed x age of a found monster of its kind on its platform is that one, and dropped.
Each remaining track is walked on at its velocity (standing under 15 units/s), turning back at its platform's walk edges.
Her memory's entries seen within 2 s are added where they were seen; all returned as Monsters.

not_done: The scene locator only runs at 1366x768 with a calibrated plate model and drawable map art; 1920x1080, the simulator and maps whose art can't be drawn use the minimap-dot path.
A place in the right map but wrong within it (the minimap picture found at a wrong place) isn't caught by placecheck.
One rope-top hang in six measured (her dot 14.8 under the top) still reads as standing on the platform.
Whether the game takes a portal while she is in the air isn't known (the simulator does).

Other players' reach (REACH_X 400, REACH_DY 100) is a guess; in game, whose minimap marker is drawn on top and the party, guild and buddy colours are unchecked (README, Other players: To check in game).
FEET_SNAP (a monster's exact feet snapping to a platform) hasn't been checked in game.
FACING_HEADING stays off until the planner's turn allowance is worked out per second.
Monsters that hop are still predicted on their own platform; the navigator flags maps where a threatening one hops.
UNSEEN_S (2 s) and KILL_NEAR's margin past 18-25 units are guesses.
Pictures gamedata can't decode yet are drawn opaque and left out of the map art's static mask.
